headline: A signature-protected CMP message fills an omitted sender with the signer's subject.
summary: pki.cmp.build refused a signature-protected PKIMessage that omitted header.sender, though a receiver holds that sender to the signer certificate's subject (RFC 9483 sec. 3.1), which is a value the builder already knows. It now fills an omitted sender with the signer's subject, the same way it fills an omitted transactionID or senderNonce.

Changed: pki.cmp.build fills a header sender the caller omits under signature protection with the signer certificate's subject (RFC 9483 sec. 3.1), so a message built without one is receivable rather than refused. A sender the caller states is left as given, matching the signer or not. A signer certificate with an empty subject names itself by a subjectAltName entry, which the builder cannot choose for the caller, so an omitted sender there is still refused with cmp/bad-input. MAC-protected messages carry no signer and are unchanged.
